sentences.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption examines ways to manage information technology contractors while reducing corruption risks and achieving project goals.
sentences.support: provide insight into the diverse range of strategies and tactics used by organisations to minimise corruption and opportunistic behaviour

sentences.text: It draws on discussions with executives, managers and auditors from public and private organisations about their contracting controls.
sentences.support: The Commission spoke with chief executive officers (CEOs), operations managers, IT managers, project managers and auditors

sentences.text: The Commission reports that its investigations linked corruption opportunities to inadequate attention to basic controls over projects and contractors.
sentences.support: the Commission’s investigations and public inquiries have found that the opportunities and motivation for corrupt behaviour occurred

sentences.text: Its guidance centres on five areas: business cases, separation of design and development, contractor selection, project supervision and exit planning.
sentences.support: all of these organisations pay close attention to the following five broad levers.

findings.quote: Contractors are able to manipulate their continued employment in the absence of an effective exit strategy.

notes: The introductory Insights derived from effective organisations section provides an overview of the five control areas. No numbered formal recommendations list.
